events.title: Uber marks the start of its New York service
events.body: In a 4 May 2011 announcement, Uber described a New York launch dinner held the previous evening to mark the start of its city service.
events.angle: App-booked services are entering the historical market. Consider where your network can serve passengers reliably; simulated fares and rival valuations are game values.

events.title: Early Uber riders appear in London
events.body: Uber described its first London test riders on 14 June 2012, while explicitly saying that the service was still in research mode ahead of launch.
events.angle: The city is entering the app-booking era. Expand deliberately; this historical test announcement does not change the simulated market by itself.

events.title: Uber formally launches in Bengaluru
events.body: Uber announced its official Bengaluru launch on 2 October 2013, following earlier testing in the city.
events.angle: New app-based competition is part of this city’s historical setting. In Fareforge, review coverage and service quality; fictional rivals still follow the game economy.

events.title: TfL declines to renew Uber’s London licence
events.body: Transport for London announced it would not issue Uber London a new private-hire operator licence when its existing licence expired. This was a licensing decision, not an immediate shutdown; the appeal process allowed continued operation.
events.angle: Licensing and operator standards shaped the real market. Review your team and fleet; Fareforge does not reproduce the legal appeal or impose an actual licence penalty.

events.title: Toyota launches the JPN Taxi
events.body: Toyota introduced its JPN Taxi on 23 October 2017 and made it available through Toyota and Toyopet dealers in Japan.
events.angle: The campaign’s 2017 JPN Taxi vehicle becomes available in this era. Its price, capacity, and performance in Fareforge are gameplay values.

events.title: Grab acquires Uber’s Southeast Asian business
events.body: The transaction completed on 26 March 2018, with Uber receiving a 27.5% stake in Grab. In its later September decision, Singapore’s competition regulator found that the deal substantially reduced competition in Singapore.
events.angle: Consolidation is part of this campaign’s setting. Fareforge’s acquisition rules and fictional rival prices are separate from the real transaction.

events.title: Lyft prices its IPO at US$72 a share
events.body: Lyft’s prospectus dated 28 March 2019 set an initial public offering price of US$72 per Class A share, with the ticker LYFT on Nasdaq. This is the offering price, not the first trading day’s closing price.
events.angle: A real historical market reference is now available in Finance. It does not reprice or rename Fareforge’s fictional companies.

events.title: Uber sets US$45 IPO price
events.body: Uber priced its initial public offering at US$45 per share on 9 May 2019. Its announcement scheduled trading on the New York Stock Exchange under UBER for the following day.
events.angle: Compare the dated historical reference in Finance with the separate simulated market. No public Uber share quotation is shown before this offering.

events.title: India announces a nationwide lockdown
events.body: On 24 March 2020, the government announced a 21-day nationwide lockdown effective from 25 March as part of its COVID-19 response.
events.angle: Fareforge models a 2020 demand shock and a one-time 52% fall in fictional rival prices. Those percentages are game rules, not observed real company share-price changes.

events.title: JapanTaxi and MOV give way to GO
events.body: The new GO taxi app launched on 1 September 2020, bringing together JapanTaxi and MOV. Its initial service covered 11 areas in Japan.
events.angle: App networks and dispatch reach were changing. Review your hub connections; this news does not automatically merge any player or rival company.

events.title: Uber reports a divided pandemic year
events.body: In its fourth-quarter 2020 results, released on 10 February 2021, Uber reported Mobility gross bookings down 50% year over year, while Delivery gross bookings rose 130% on a reported basis.
events.source: Uber · Q4 and full-year 2020 results, 10 February 2021
events.angle: This is an operating-results comparison, not a stock-price fall. Fareforge’s commuter and parcel work represent different demand streams; their in-game balance is fictional.

events.title: Namma Yatri launches in Bengaluru
events.body: A contemporary report described Namma Yatri’s launch on 1 November 2022. The auto-booking app connected passengers with drivers and did not deduct a ride commission, according to drivers interviewed in the report.
events.angle: Driver-direct booking provides historical context for an alternative business model. Fareforge’s subscription fee is invented; the article does not establish a ₹25/day launch fee.

events.title: San Francisco expands paid driverless service
events.body: California’s utilities regulator approved additional operating authority for Cruise and Waymo on 10 August 2023, allowing both to charge for driverless passenger rides in San Francisco at any time of day.
events.angle: This records the approval at that moment in history, not permanent permission or a claim about later operations. Fareforge vehicle abilities remain game abstractions.

events.title: New York begins congestion-zone tolling
events.body: New York’s Congestion Relief Zone began charging entry tolls on 5 January 2025. The zone covers Manhattan south of and including 60th Street, with specified roadway exclusions.
events.source: MTA · Congestion Relief Zone launch information
events.angle: The launch belongs to 2025, not 2024. Fareforge does not reproduce the toll schedule; review your network with this historical change in mind.
